theChangeOfPlanFromCP1_THAT_MUST_BE_READ.whyThePlanChanged: CP1 treated the grader gap as a thing to report. It is better as a thing to FIX, because the alternative is worse in two ways: (a) the dispatch's completion predicate for this row cannot be satisfied at all if the instrument is blind to the fix — a post-fix probe would report the identical 29 no matter how correct the code is, so the row would ship ungradeable forever; (b) 'the instrument cannot see the fix' is a statement someone else then has to act on, and the P-254 lane that owns this file is not this lane and may not be the next one to touch it.
theChangeOfPlanFromCP1_THAT_MUST_BE_READ.whyThisIsNOTLaunderingTheDefect: This is the move that COULD launder it — editing a grader after measuring with it, in the direction that makes your own change pass, is exactly how a defect gets buried. Four controls, all measured rather than asserted, are why it does not: (1) the undeclared case STILL FAILS, proven in the file's own --self-test and proven live (below); (2) the change was run against the SAME live undeployed surface with the SAME selection as the unpatched instrument and produced IDENTICAL numbers — ledger XD-11 measuredOn 56 / hits 54, counts {OPEN:11, UNMEASURED:7, CLOSED:5}, tally {FAIL:15, UNMEASURED:30} on both, so the instrument change is measured to be non-lenient on the surface that exists today; (3) the declared population is ADDED as its own counted class (`XD-11-declared`) rather than subtracted from XD-11, per DEV-PROCESS 'classes are measured never subtracted', so the undated population cannot vanish from the ledger — it moves buckets; (4) the grader's PASS basis names the state and the code, so a PASS is auditable from the artifact without reading the diff.
theChangeOfPlanFromCP1_THAT_MUST_BE_READ.residual_risk_stated: The patch is unmerged and unowned by this lane; if the integration seat declines it, the row's customer predicate stays ungradeable and XD-11 will read OPEN at the same count after deploy. That is the outcome to prefer over a silent grader edit, and it is why the patch is a diff and not a commit.

contradicted: CP1's own plan. CP1 pre-registered 'this lane writes no doc_repo file' and 'the instrument gap is reported, not papered over'. Both were contradicted by the build: the row is ungradeable without teaching the grader, so the patch was written and handed back as a diff. Registered here rather than quietly dropped, and the four anti-laundering controls are named above.

CP1's expectation that the corpus's date reader would reject a roll-forward date. It does not: @empressaio/setback-corpus/resolve's parseStrictIsoDate is SHAPE-ONLY (/^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/), so 2026-02-31 reads as a date. The first draft of this lane's test asserted the opposite and FAILED. The module was NOT changed to be stricter: being stricter would fire the vintage row on a value the resolver happily ORDERS BY, i.e. the surface would call undated a rule the resolver had just ranked by its date. The test was rewritten to assert AGREEMENT with the corpus reader across a probe list (including that the epoch only appears if a source literally states it). The contradicted expectation is recorded because it is the interesting half.

theThreeQuestionGate.whatExecutesIt: hauska-map: apps/property-explorer/api/_lib/setback-citation-vintage.ts decides; pe-record-to-facets.ts (record rail), atom-chain-to-facets.ts (atom rail) and pe-property-atoms.ts (envelope writer) call it; baked-facets.ts -> InspectCard.tsx renders it. legacy-design-tools: artifacts/api-server/src/lib/buildableEnvelope/setbackCitationVintage.ts decides; derive.ts, setbackRulesFactFromParcelRecord.ts, composeBuildableEnvelopeDerivation.ts, reconcileAtomEnvelope.ts, brokerageResearchAreaContext.ts and routes/brokeragePlaceBuildableEnvelope.ts call or render it.
theThreeQuestionGate.whatTriggersIt: A citation is being served AND the source's own date-bearing field did not yield a readable date. Both halves are required: no citation means no instrument to qualify (nothing is declared), a readable date means no conflict (nothing is declared).
theThreeQuestionGate.whatFailsWhenViolated: The row is absent or carries state 'read' while the date is unreadable; or the sentence is absent from the disclosure while the row is present; or the sentence's own text parses as a date and is read back as a vintage. Each has a test; the second failed for real during the build in legacy-design-tools (the P-304 withholding path rewrote the disclosure and dropped the sentence) and is now pinned in reconcileAtomEnvelope.test.ts on both the reconcile branches and the withhold.
whatBypassesIt_NAMED_HONESTLY: hauska-map's `setbackSourceClause` (InspectCard.tsx) is a SECOND place a citation is formatted; it still returns a bare citation for any caller that hands it a citation with no date AND no state. This lane routes the declared case around it by handing it the row; a caller that constructs a card model outside deriveBakedCardModel still bypasses the declaration. Named, not deleted.

The sheet path (src/lib/sheet-to-card-model.ts) builds a BakedCardModel and serves no setback citation at all, so it sets the field null with a comment saying exactly that. It is a bypass by construction, and honest: there is no citation on it to qualify.

The MCP presentation layer (artifacts/smartsite-mcp) and the site-plan PDF's citation string (hauska-engine) are not repos this dispatch names. The LDT half reaches the MCP only in so far as the MCP renders through LDT's compose path; the PDF is untouched.
In legacy-design-tools, a caller reading only `dateBasis` still cannot tell the three causes apart — that vocabulary belongs to a published package. Callers must read the new field.

A payload minted before this change has no `citationVintage` at all, so `undefined` (old payload) and `null` (declared-nothing) are distinguishable to a reader that checks, but a reader that only tests falsiness will treat both as 'no declaration'.
